resale_co.how_to_apply: No Township Certificate of Occupancy is needed for a sale since January 1, 2026. The seller still needs the smoke / CO / 911 house numbering inspection from the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (see fire section) and County Health Department water and septic certifications, all at least 10 days before closing.

evidence.quote: Please be advised that, effective January 1, 2026 , Hopewell Township, Cumberland County will no longer require local Certificate of Occupancy (CO) or Smoke Certification inspections in connection with the sale of residential properties.

Notwithstanding the above, compliance inspections for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide (CO) detectors, and 911 house numbering remain mandatory and must be completed satisfactorily prior to the closing of title .

Notwithstanding the above, certifications for drinking water quality and septic system functionality remain mandatory and must be completed to the satisfaction of the Cumberland County Health Department prior to the closing of title .

resale_co.notes: Hopewell Township's 'Buying or Selling Your Home in Hopewell' notice and its Housing, Code Enforcement and Property Maintenance page both say that from January 1, 2026 the Township no longer requires a local Certificate of Occupancy or smoke certification inspection for residential sales. Smoke, CO and 911 house numbering inspections are still mandatory before closing and are now done by the City of Bridgeton Fire Department. Water quality and septic certifications from the Cumberland County Health Department are also still required, with records submitted at least 10 days before closing. Rentals remain under the Township's landlord registration and inspection rules (Ordinance 15-10), and vacant and foreclosed homes must be registered (Ordinance 2024-13); those are not resale items.

requirements: Hopewell adds a 911 house numbering check to the Bridgeton smoke/CO inspection; inspections must be scheduled and passed at least 10 days before the closing date
Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Hopewell Township as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: Since January 1, 2026 the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's Fire Marshal's Office runs the resale smoke / CO (and 911 house numbering) inspections for Hopewell Township; the Township says they must be passed at least 10 days before closing. The Bridgeton online application lists Hopewell Township. Fees, lead time and the 90-day validity come from the Bridgeton Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025). The Hopewell / Stow Creek Fire Department (751 Roadstown Road) is the volunteer fire company and does not issue the certificate.
